PART I
Item 1.Business
Overview
Acme Robotics Corp. designs, manufactures and services industrial robots and warehouse automation systems. The Company was founded in 2009 and is headquartered in Columbus, Ohio. We sell to manufacturers, third-party logistics providers and retailers in North America and Europe. We operate in two reportable segments: Industrial Automation and Warehouse Systems.
Segments and Products
Our Industrial Automation segment sells ArcLine robotic welding cells, PalletPro palletizing robots and the related controllers, vision systems and software licenses. Our Warehouse Systems segment sells ShelfRunner autonomous mobile robots, which move inventory between storage and packing stations, together with the FleetView orchestration software that coordinates fleets of up to 2,000 robots in a single facility. Software and service contracts represented 21% of total revenue in 2024 compared with 18% in 2023.
Customers
We sold products to more than 900 customers in 2024. Our largest customer, a global e-commerce retailer, accounted for 14% of total revenue in 2024 and 11% in 2023. No other customer accounted for more than 10% of total revenue. As of December 31, 2024, our order backlog was $612.4 million, compared with $498.0 million as of December 31, 2023. We expect to recognize approximately 70% of the December 31, 2024 backlog as revenue during 2025.
Research and Development
Research and development expense was $96.3 million in 2024, $84.7 million in 2023 and $77.1 million in 2022. Our engineering teams focus on motion control, machine vision and fleet software. As of December 31, 2024, we held 412 issued patents and had 138 patent applications pending worldwide.
Competition
The markets for industrial robots and warehouse automation are highly competitive. We compete with large diversified industrial companies and with venture-backed robotics start-ups. We believe the principal competitive factors are reliability, total cost of ownership, ease of integration with existing warehouse management systems and the breadth of the service network.
Human Capital
As of December 31, 2024, we had approximately 3,400 full-time employees, of whom approximately 1,150 worked in manufacturing, 820 in research and development, 760 in field service and the remainder in sales and administration. None of our employees in the United States are represented by a labor union. Voluntary employee turnover was 9.8% in 2024.

Item 1A.Risk Factors
Our business is subject to many risks. The risks described below are not the only risks we face.
We depend on a single supplier for harmonic drive gearboxes. A single supplier located in Japan provides the harmonic drive gearboxes used in approximately 70% of the robots we shipped in 2024. We do not have a long-term supply agreement with this supplier. Any interruption in its operations, including as a result of natural disasters, export restrictions or capacity constraints, could delay our shipments for six months or more while we qualify an alternative source.
Our revenue is concentrated among a small number of large customers. Our ten largest customers accounted for 46% of total revenue in 2024. The loss of, or a significant reduction in orders from, any of these customers could materially reduce our revenue and profitability.
Tariffs could increase our costs. We manufacture a majority of our robot arms in Monterrey, Mexico and import electronic components from Asia. Changes in trade policy, including new tariffs on components imported into the United States or Mexico, could increase our cost of revenue and reduce our gross margin.
Rising interest rates could reduce customer demand. Many of our customers finance automation projects. Higher interest rates increase the cost of those projects and have caused, and may in the future cause, customers to delay or cancel orders.
Security breaches could disrupt our operations and expose us to liability. Our robots connect to customer networks and to our cloud-based FleetView software. A breach of our systems or our products could interrupt customer operations, result in the loss of confidential information and expose us to claims and regulatory penalties.

Item 1B.Unresolved Staff Comments
None.
Item 1C.Cybersecurity
Our Chief Information Security Officer leads our cybersecurity program and reports to the Audit Committee of the Board of Directors at least quarterly. We engage an independent firm to perform penetration testing of our corporate systems and of the FleetView platform each year. We did not identify any cybersecurity incident in 2024 that materially affected, or is reasonably likely to materially affect, our business strategy, results of operations or financial condition.
Item 2.Properties
Our headquarters and primary research facility in Columbus, Ohio occupies approximately 220,000 square feet, which we own. We lease a 310,000 square foot manufacturing plant in Monterrey, Mexico under a lease that expires in 2031, and we lease sales and service offices in Chicago, Atlanta, Rotterdam and Munich. We believe our facilities are adequate for our current needs.
Item 3.Legal Proceedings
In March 2024, Gantry Dynamics LLC filed a complaint against the Company in the United States District Court for the District of Delaware alleging that our ShelfRunner robots infringe two of its patents. We believe the claims are without merit and intend to defend ourselves vigorously. We have not recorded an accrual for this matter because we do not believe a loss is probable.

Item 5.Market for Registrant's Common Equity, Related Stockholder Matters and Issuer Purchases of Equity Securities
Our common stock trades on the Nasdaq Global Select Market under the symbol ZZACM. As of February 14, 2025, there were approximately 1,150 holders of record of our common stock. In the third quarter of 2024 our Board of Directors initiated a quarterly cash dividend of $0.12 per share. In October 2024, our Board of Directors authorized a share repurchase program of up to $50 million. During the fourth quarter of 2024 we repurchased 210,000 shares at an average price of $68.40 per share.

Item 7.Management's Discussion and Analysis of Financial Condition and Results of Operations
Overview
Total revenue increased 13.6% to $1,284.6 million in 2024 from $1,130.5 million in 2023, driven primarily by higher ShelfRunner volumes in our Warehouse Systems segment and price increases in our Industrial Automation segment. Gross margin improved to 38.2% in 2024 from 36.9% in 2023 as a result of a richer software mix and lower freight costs. Net income was $112.8 million, or $2.31 per diluted share, compared with $88.1 million, or $1.79 per diluted share, in 2023.
Revenue by Segment

Industrial Automation revenue increased 9.7% primarily due to price increases averaging 6% and higher demand from automotive suppliers. Warehouse Systems revenue increased 21.1% as the number of ShelfRunner robots shipped grew to 6,850 in 2024 from 5,420 in 2023.
Operating Expenses
Selling, general and administrative expense increased to $214.5 million in 2024 from $198.2 million in 2023, primarily due to investments in our European sales organization. Research and development expense increased to $96.3 million from $84.7 million as we expanded our fleet software team.
Acme Robotics Corp. | 2024 Form 10-K | 14
Liquidity and Capital Resources
As of December 31, 2024, we had cash and cash equivalents of $284.7 million. We have a $400 million senior secured revolving credit facility that matures in 2028, under which $75 million was outstanding as of December 31, 2024. Borrowings bear interest at a variable rate based on SOFR plus a margin of 1.50% to 2.25%. Net cash provided by operating activities was $168.9 million in 2024. Capital expenditures were $41.2 million in 2024, primarily for the expansion of our Monterrey plant, and we expect capital expenditures of $45 million to $55 million in 2025. We believe our cash, cash flows from operations and available borrowing capacity will be sufficient to meet our liquidity needs for at least the next twelve months.
Critical Accounting Estimates
Revenue from multi-element arrangements that include robots, software licenses and service contracts is allocated based on standalone selling prices. Estimating standalone selling prices for bundled FleetView software requires significant judgment. Warranty reserves are estimated based on historical failure rates, which were 1.7% of units in 2024.
Item 7A.Quantitative and Qualitative Disclosures About Market Risk
Interest Rate Risk. Borrowings under our revolving credit facility bear interest at variable rates. Based on the $75 million outstanding as of December 31, 2024, a hypothetical 100 basis point increase in interest rates would increase our annual interest expense by approximately $0.8 million.
Foreign Currency Risk. A significant portion of our manufacturing costs is denominated in Mexican pesos. A hypothetical 10% strengthening of the Mexican peso against the U.S. dollar would have increased our 2024 cost of revenue by approximately $6.5 million. We do not currently hedge this exposure.

Note 2. Revenue Recognition
We recognize revenue from robot sales when control transfers to the customer, which is generally upon shipment. Revenue from FleetView software subscriptions and service contracts is recognized ratably over the contract term, which is typically three to five years. Deferred revenue was $142.6 million as of December 31, 2024 and $118.3 million as of December 31, 2023.
